You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 0.76 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal (weak); Ip = 12 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 10000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 12 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 6800 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 22000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weakest excitation; Ip = 8 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 22000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 10 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 10000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 12 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 10000 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:

S2      0.558   0.563    11.2       -    0.0457  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       2.24    2.26    35.4   0.329     0.228  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S4      0.334   0.339    8.95       -   0.00508  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok

S6      0.459   0.462     6.1       -    0.0211  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:

    },

    },

    }

  }
 ]
}

reply.reasoning:
*   Target: `vout_min >= 1.8 V`, `vout_max <= 3.6 V`, `ripple <= 0.05 V`, `tup <= 0.4 s`, `settled <= 0.02 V`.
    *   Piezo: Sinusoidal current source, $C_p = 25\text{ nF}$. Open-circuit voltage is low ($\approx 0.76\text{ V}$ amplitude), meaning we need an efficient boost (like SSHI).
    *   Best design so far (`c0048`, SSHI Full-Bridge):
        *   `vavg` is high ($\approx 3.3\text{ V}$), passing `vout_min` and `vout_max`.
        *   `tup` is good ($\approx 0.14\text{ s}$), passing `startup`.
        *   Problem: `ripple` on S3 ($56\text{ mV} > 50\text{ mV}$) and `settled` on S4 ($31\text{ mV} > 20\text{ mV}$).
        *   The `settled` error on S4 means the voltage is still rising/falling at 0.8 s. The time constant $\tau = R_L \cdot C_{out}$ is likely too large.
        *   The `ripple` error on S3 means the storage capacitor $C_{out}$ is too small to maintain stability under the load/pulse combination.

    *   Wait, if $C_{out}$ is too small, ripple increases. If $C_{out}$ is too large, the settled time increases (it takes longer to reach steady state).
    *   This is a classic tradeoff. We need to find a better way to filter the output without just increasing $C_{out}$ linearly.
    *   The `SSHI_FullBridge` (c0048) uses a bridge and a Zener. The SSHI part (L1, S1, G1) flips the piezo voltage to increase the charge extracted per cycle.
    *   The failing conditions are:
        *   S4 (weakest): `settled` fail ($0.031\text{ V}$). This suggests the system hasn't reached equilibrium by 0.8 s.
        *   S3 (strongest/lightest load): `ripple` fail ($0.056\text{ V}$). This suggests the ripple is slightly too high.

    *   To fix `settled` (S4), we need a faster response. $\tau = R_L \cdot C_{out}$. Since $R_L$ is fixed (for S4, $R_L = 22\text{ M}\Omega$), $C_{out}$ must be smaller.
    *   To fix `ripple` (S3), we need a larger $C_{out}$ or better filtering. Since $R_L$ is larger for S3 ($22\text{ M}\Omega$), ripple should actually be *lower* than for S2 ($6.8\text{ M}\Omega$), unless the pulse energy from the SSHI is much higher.
    *   Looking at c0048: $C_{out} = 366\text{ nF}$.
        For S4: $R_L = 22\text{ M}\Omega$. $\tau = 22\text{ M} \cdot 366\text{ n} \approx 8.05\text{ s}$. This is way too slow to settle in 0.8 s!
        For S2: $R_L = 6.8\text{ M}\Omega$. $\tau = 6.8\text{ M} \cdot 366\text{ n} \approx 2.48\text{ s}$. Still slow.
    *   Wait, why did S1, S2, S5, S6 pass `settled` but S4 didn't?
        S1: $R_L = 10\text{ M}\Omega$.
        S2: $R_L = 6.8\text{ M}\Omega$.
        S4: $R_L = 22\text{ M}\Omega$.
        The time constant is much larger for S4.

    *   We need a way to decouple the storage capacitance (for ripple) from the load's settling time. However, the load is directly across the capacitor in this topology.
    *   Alternatively, we can use a smaller $C_{out}$ to fix the `settled` time and find a way to reduce the ripple.
    *   Wait, if we reduce $C_{out}$, the ripple on S3 will likely get *worse*.
    *   Is there a way to reduce the ripple without increasing $C_{out}$? An LC filter (like in `c0061`) was tried, but it made `settled` worse on S4.

    *   Actually, let's look at the `settled` condition: `dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)| <= 0.02 V`.
    *   For S4 in `c0048`, `dv = 0.031 V`.
    *   The voltage is likely still charging because the piezo source is very weak.
    *   If we want it to settle faster, we can't just reduce $C_{out}$ because we need it for the ripple.
    *   But wait, look at the `vavg` for S4 in `c0048`: $3.3\text{ V}$. It's already at the Zener limit.
    *   If the voltage is already at $3.3\text{ V}$ (Zener), and the Zener is conducting, the "settling" is actually the Zener clamp fighting the charger.
    *   Actually, if `vmax` is $3.3\text{ V}$ and `vavg` is $3.3\text{ V}$, the Zener is definitely clamping. The ripple is the key.

    *   The `S3 ripple` failure ($56\text{ mV}$) is very close to the limit ($50\text{ mV}$).
    *   The `S4 settled` failure ($31\text{ mV}$) is also close.
    *   Maybe we just need a slightly different storage arrangement.
    *   What if we use a capacitor-multiplier or a different rectification stage?
    *   Actually, a simple way to reduce ripple without increasing $C_{out}$ too much is to use a second-stage filter or a different bridge.
    *   But let's try a different SSHI approach. The current one is a Full-Bridge SSHI.
    *   What if we use a "Half-Bridge" (charge pump) style SSHI? Or a different inductor placement?

    *   Wait, let's look at the `S4 settled` again. `vavg = 3.3V`, `vmax = 3.3V`. If it's clamped by the Zener, the ripple is very small ($11\text{ mV}$). The `dv` is the difference between the means of two windows.
    *   If the voltage is still climbing toward $3.3\text{ V}$ from $0\text{ V}$, and it hits the Zener around $0.7\text{ s}$, the mean of $0.6-0.7$ will be lower than the mean of $0.7-0.8$.
    *   To fix this, we need `tup` to be even faster or the voltage to reach the clamp earlier.
    *   `tup` for S4 is $0.244\text{ s}$, which is well within $0.4\text{ s}$.
    *   Wait, if it reaches $1.8\text{ V}$ at $0.244\text{ s}$, why is it still "not settled" at $0.7\text{ s}$?
    *   Because it's continuing to rise from $1.8\text{ V}$ up to $3.3\text{ V}$.
    *   To settle faster, we need to reach $3.3\text{ V}$ (the clamp) faster.
    *   To reach $3.3\text{ V}$ faster, we need *less* capacitance $C_{out}$.
    *   But if we decrease $C_{out}$, the ripple on S3 will increase.
    *   S3 ripple is $56\text{ mV}$. If we decrease $C_{out}$ to fix S4 settled, S3 ripple will likely exceed $60\text{ mV}$.

    *   Is there a way to reduce ripple on S3 while keeping $C_{out}$ small?
    *   S3 has the *lightest* load ($R_L = 22\text{ M}\Omega$). Ripple is $\Delta V \approx \frac{I \cdot \Delta t}{C_{out}}$.
    *   The ripple on S3 is caused by the charge pulses from the SSHI.
    *   If we can make the pulses more frequent or smaller, the ripple will decrease.
    *   The SSHI pulses occur every half-period ($5\text{ ms}$ at $100\text{ Hz}$).
    *   Maybe we can use a different output filter? An RC filter might work, but it would drop the voltage.

    *   Let's try to refine the SSHI structure.
    *   Instead of a full bridge, maybe use a different arrangement of diodes to lower the drop or improve efficiency? (Though DSCH is already quite good).
    *   What if we use a "Parallel SSHI" or a different inductor-switch config?
    *   Another idea: the Zener `DZ33` clamps at $3.3\text{ V}$. If we use a slightly higher Zener or no Zener and a different way to limit voltage? No, the rules say we must use the provided components.

    *   S3 ripple: $56\text{ mV}$ (limit $50\text{ mV}$)
    *   S4 settled: $31\text{ mV}$ (limit $20\text{ mV}$)
    *   The `vavg` is $3.3\text{ V}$ for both.
    *   If I reduce $C_{out}$ by, say, 20%:
        *   `settled` (S4) should improve (faster rise to $3.3\text{ V}$).
        *   `ripple` (S3) will increase (probably to $\sim 70\text{ mV}$).
    *   This is a deadlock. I need a way to lower the ripple without increasing $C_{out}$.
